title: The Influence of Local Pamidronate Application on Alveolar Dimensional Preservation after Tooth Extraction—An Animal Experimental Study*
authors: Kauffmann F, Höhne C, Assaf AT, Vollkommer T, Semmusch J, Reitmeier A, Stein JM, Heiland M, Smeets R, Rutkowski R. Int J Mol Sci. 2020 May;21(10):3616. doi: 10.3390/ijms21103616.
supports: Pre-clinical study from the botiss cerabone (sintered bovine bone) literature list — the product featured in it, which is not the same as the study being about the product, so check the design and the comparator before citing it as product evidence. Abstract, verbatim (no separate conclusion section): “The aim of this randomized, controlled animal exploratory trial was to investigate the influence of local application of aminobisphosphonate pamidronate during the socket preservation procedure . Mandibular premolars were extracted in five Göttingen minipig s. Two animals underwent socket preservation using BEGO OSS (n = 8 sockets) and three animals using BEGO OSS + Pamifos (15 mg) (n = 12 sockets). After jaw impression, cast models (baseline, eight weeks postoperative) were digitized using an inLab X5 scanne r (Dentsply Sirona) and the generated STL data were superimposed and analyzed with GOM Inspect 2018 (GOM, Braunschweig). After 16 weeks, the lower jaws were prepared and examined using standard histological methods.
